exemplarMoves: Swap the generic noun for the world-register noun only where the scene's engine uses it (chalk -> alchemical chalk, blue -> Dalaran blue).
Let the POV's trade pick the verbs and the nouns (a ranger reads dead ground, sightlines, spacing, tack).
Make a plain answer usable on the ground: streets, doors, ovens, carts, not category labels ('Say it in streets').
Keep cadence: substitute and lightly extend, never replace a clipped paragraph with a descriptive one.
Dialogue picks up local register and shared context; the world arrives in the beat between quotes, not inside the speech.

openingThird.note: Scene 1 is already richly anchored: inn sign, horseshoe, wheelwright, drawknife, well rope, windlass, storehouse. Surgical only.

middleThird.note: Scene 2 cellar and interview already carry strong material (turnips, darn, shaving glass, cellar slot). Convocation interior is the thinnest register.

finalThird.note: Ride south (human country, farm) leans on generic farmland nouns; carter's price is a generic 'penny'; Convocation chamber is unnamed.
